I would beg to differ. Under the current syntax, " What if choosing YOUR
highest capacity vampire caused YOUR pool to now be greater than someone
YOU wanted to Parity Shift?" Obviously, he is asking if he had both
Ancient Influence and Parity Shift in his hand, then he could Ancient Influence
a vampire who was not his eldest vampire, so that he would still have less
pool than another player who he would then Parity Shift.

Although, now that I think about it, there is another possibility. If you
had 3 pool, were holding a Ancient Influence in your hand, had both Sheldon and
Tusk, the Talebearer, in play, your prey had 5 pool, the top card of your deck
was a parity shift (you know this because of Tusk's special ability), you have
vote lock, your prey's largest vampire is a 5 cap, and there are five players
on the table. You could call the Ancient Influence with Tusk, select Tusk,
thus netting you one pool, which brings your total to 4 pool, and allowing you
to cycle to the Parity Shift, that you call with Sheldon and oust your prey by
moving his five pool (five players= five pool) to your pool. You gain a victory
point and are now back in the game with 15 pool. If it was written that you
had to choose your largest vampire, then you couldn't do this and would now have
a pool of 8 and a nearly worthless Parity Shift in your hand (worthless in that
you would have to play it on some other Methuselah than your prey).

Comments Welcome,
Norman S. Brown Jr.

Just to jump in here for a minute, but is this the way Parity
Shift actually works? We had a fairly lengthy discussion about it in our
local group about the wording, and came to the conclusion that the amount
of pool you could allocate due to Parity Shift was limited by both the
number of players in the game *and* the amount of pool by which your
totals differed. For instance, in this situation, you could only Parity
Shift for 1 pool, as the target had only 1 more pool than you did.

Relevant text:
"Choose a Methuselah who has more blood in his or her pool than
you do. {Allocate X of that pool among the other remaining Methuselahs
(including you), where X is the number of Methuselahs in the game}."

Were we wrong?

>I logically look at each and every card in terms of functionality.

OK, let me give you a quickie on functionality.

Making Ancient Influence playable more than once per game is pretty
much handing big vampire decks pool gain that is more powerful than
Minion Tap/5th. Imagine a deck with a ready Arika and two other
Ventrue calling three of these per turn? That's 6 pool *PER ACTION*,
not to mention anything snagged from Voter Captivation. Minion
Tap/5th, in contrast, would gain you only 9 pool (Arika can't 5th
herself, need to use Democritus), and you can only do that once per
turn. It would be... ridiculously abusive.

As far as the wording goes - it was written the way it was written,
back long ago. There is NO gameplay-based reason to change the way it
is written. Several other people have pointed out corner-case
scenarios where one might, in fact, choose other that one's
highest-cap vampire. Rare, yes, but of such corner-cases are winning
strategic plays made... the people who NOTICE. The wording is not at
all unclear - it says "each Methuselah may choose a ready vampire he
or she controls". The wording is, in fact, clearly deliberate. Given
the existence of cards such as Parity Shift (from the same set and
timeframe), it seems highly likely that such a "corner case" occurred
to the designers, as well, and they intentionally left a loophole for
clever players.

Messages.Author: Jack Crow
Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
On Fri, 01 Jun 2001 01:55:45 GMT, no...@nowhere.com (Jack Crow) wrote:

>The Succubus club only allows the transfer of objects in-game and
>specifically cards from your hand or in-play, and pool. These trades
>can only be traded between the Succubus club owner and another
>methuselah one at a time (if you look at the transaction model). No
>other agreements are enforced by the rules, so are considered "verbal"
>agreements (see next paragraph).

"verbal" agreements are the primary function of the Succubus Club when
it is included in a deck - typically giving pool, cards, minions, etc.
for favors. I don't see it being a -major- issue to code, however, as
it's a simple matter of specifying valid targets to "move".

However, see next paragraph.

>A common question is whether or not I will have a way for players to
>communicate via chat messages. I see no reason to implement a cheesy
>chat client at this time, since IRC clients provide more sophisticated
>and appropriate functionality.

This is a fatal flaw. You MUST include something integrated into the
client, no matter how primitive, and even if it only allows chat to
one "central" public area with no bells, no whistles, no nothing. The
-real- game revolves around communication, and if there is none, then
the game will be only a pale shadow of "real" V:TES.

Suggesting that players use IRC clients (or anything else) in the
background is a typical coder-centric perspective, and a bad, BAD
mistake. Joe Average wants something that is functional out of the
box, not something that forces him to download an IRC client as well
just to talk to other people while he's playing.

Look at Yahoo!'s games area, for example - their "chat" function is
about as primitive as it gets, yet you can enter most games and find
table-talk merrily going on. People want to be social, and they won't
want to screw around with IRC clients and external programs and
hopping back and forth just to do it.

>Errata will be implemented as it occurs. Coding an entirely new set of

You haven't done this sort of thing before, have you? Time and time
again, coders attempt to make this commitment, and time and time
again, they realize what a pain it is to actually DO that sort of
thing and vanish into the middle distance, leaving the users stuck
with a white elephant. Better to leave server operators at least
REASONABLY able to edit the card database themselves, so that "house
rules" can be put in place easily... cf. the Quake I phenomenon. Yes,
I realize that some cards, such as Mind Numb and Rotschreck, produce
effects that are difficult to handle without special code, and that
can't be helped. But most cards affect basic building blocks, such as
"minion blood", "minion's current region" (ready, torpor,
uncontrolled), etc. And leaving THESE server-operator-editable would
be very wise.

...You ARE doing it client-server, right? Not peer-to-peer? It
doesn't have to be a lone-dedicated-server machine, of course, but
having one person "host" the game is a much more stable option,
especially since if ANYONE drops from the game, the game can't
continue, so putting all the eggs in one 'server' basket won't matter.
Not to mention that you can eliminate much of the potential for
cheating that way (although as always, you have to trust the host's
machine).

>My API is quite extensive in order that I may accomodate every
>possible combination of events and some that arent. My strict
>enforcement of the rules will allow games to move faster as an aim to
>reduce the need for chatter. You will be able to examine everyone's

You need to be very careful, though. Your previous comment about
action modifiers/reactions disturbed me greatly, as it indicates that
you don't actually play this game very much at ALL currently. Perhaps
in the past, but certainly not recently. We all appreciate your
efforts to create something, ... but I have also seen many people,
time and again, simply blow smoke up the public's collective asses
with vapourware that just never quite made it to a "functional" stage
for one reason or another. Sometimes totally unintentionally.

>table up close at will. Examine any card in play, at will.
>Implementing "seeing all other methuselah's hands for the rest of your
>turn" is a snap in my design. Most importantly, this client will allow
>more than 2 people to play at once (up tot 8 - 10). The max number has
>not been set yet, but will be sane (< 12) to protect against certain
>runtime problems.

The max number should really be set at 5. The game-time tends to
increase exponentially once you go higher than 5, and it is worth
noting that 6 is the lowest number of players where there is a person
whom your actions have ABSOLUTELY no effect on. In a five-player
game, you directly affect your prey and predator, and your actions or
lack thereof will indirectly affect your grandprey and grandpredator,
respectively. In a six-player game, the "ripple effect" simply
doesn't make it that far down the table, and the person who is
directly across from you can totally ignore you until the first person
is ousted. This is not a very good thing.

If nothing else, it could be made a server-side option and the default
max_clients_connected should be 5 - forcing hosts to go out of their
way to alter it.

-- Derek
Thug of Atlanta

Messages.Author: Andrew S. Davidson

On Fri, 01 Jun 2001 01:55:45 GMT, Jack Crow wrote:

>The Succubus club only allows the transfer of objects in-game and
>specifically cards from your hand or in-play, and pool. These trades
>can only be traded between the Succubus club owner and another
>methuselah one at a time (if you look at the transaction model).

I still don't see where you're getting this one-at-a-time transaction
model from. The card implies that trades within an untap phase are
binding. One reason for this would be to eliminate awkward disputes
as to who actually controls an object during a trade if one side
wanted to renege. E.g. Player A agrees to trade 3 pool and the Ivory
Bow for The Parthenon. Player B agrees and takes the pool and bow
from Player A. Player A reaches for The Parthenon but Player B then
says, "Fooled you! - I'm not going through with my end of the deal."
They now tussle over The Parthenon card and tear it into two...

To avoid this, it is best if deals are bundled and binding.

>A common question is whether or not I will have a way for players to
>communicate via chat messages. I see no reason to implement a cheesy
>chat client at this time, since IRC clients provide more sophisticated
>and appropriate functionality.

One reason to have an integrated chat client is that it would allow
you to implement Madness of the Bard using a rigorous algorithm like
Soundex.

Andrew

Well, it implies that trades are made. You make a trade (as specified/allowed

> One reason for this would be to eliminate awkward disputes

>
> To avoid this, it is best if deals are bundled and binding.

Correct, and this is how the card works.

You trade 3 pool and the Ivory Bow for the Parthenon. Before the trade,
you control 3 pool and the Ivory bow and your partner controls the Parthenon.
After the trade you control the Parthenon and your partner controls the 3
pool and the Ivory Bow.
